summary: Maine Forest Service fire lookout from 1911; 24-ft steel tower from 1914; cut down and scrapped in 2012. No source gives current public access.

facts.design: 24-foot steel tower with a house on top for the watchman (1914), replacing a wooden tower built in 1911
facts.status_note: Cut down and scrapped in 2012; a hiker later found a partly erected tower and footings on the summit

visit.trail_note: Summit reached by the West Kennebago trail; a hiker's forum post describes it as a 4.5 mile hike from the trailhead

events.note: Wooden lookout tower and station; about two and a half miles of telephone line connected it
Wooden tower replaced by a 24-foot steel tower with a house on top; Maine Memory gives an elevation of 3,705 feet
Wallace S. Houston served as watchman
State fire warden Lewis Blake and his wife spent the summer at the lookout; stationed there again in 1926
Forest Lookouts gives 18 May; the 2012 FFLA report planned a lift for Saturday 19 May, which failed; the tower was cut down and scrapped

notes_for_editor: Removal date conflict: Forest Lookouts says 18 May 2012; the FFLA 2012 report planned a lift for Saturday 19 May, which failed (the record note uses 19 May). Height conflict: 1914 records say 24 ft (Maine Memory, Forest Lookouts); a 1925 Daily Kennebec Journal letter says 40 ft; unresolved. Agency: record says Maine Forestry District; Maine Memory says Forest Service; story uses Forest Service. Today's site comes from a 2017 birder blog and an undated hiker forum post, not an official source. The forum says a communications tower was partly erected; the WebSearch summary's 80-foot figure and the 2011 report's planned destination were not verified in a page we read, so they are left out. No current access information found.
